correctness.summary: The two-sided mixed-Schatten estimate is correct. Schatten Hölder gives the universal lower bound ||[A,B]||_r<=2||A||_p||B||_q. For normal T, the polar part commutes with |T|, so X=U|T|^(r/p) and Y=|T|^(r/q) commute, multiply to T, and satisfy ||X||_p||Y||_q=||T||_r. Tensoring this split with any rank-one factorization P=[C,Z] gives [X⊗C,Y⊗Z]=T⊗P with exactly multiplicative Schatten norms. On a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, a finite-rank normal T and T⊗P have the same nonzero spectral multiplicities and infinite-dimensional zero eigenspaces, hence are unitarily equivalent; the same applies to normal compact T with infinite-dimensional kernel. Dykema–Figiel–Weiss–Wodzicki explicitly record Brown's obstruction and Anderson's converse: a finite-rank nonzero-trace element can be a single [S_p,S_q] commutator exactly on the strict side 1/p+1/q<1/2. This yields the claimed positive-target phase transition.

limitations: The constant c_{p,q}=Gamma_{p,q}(P) is implicit and no sharp constant is proved.
The infinite-rank extension requires infinite-dimensional kernel because the tensor carrier changes kernel multiplicity.
The exact nonexistence phase statement is only for nonzero positive finite-rank targets, using their nonzero trace.
Anderson (1986) could not be read in text form despite authorized retrieval and remains an explicit older-prior risk.

originality.summary: The Brown–Anderson existence threshold, rank-one commutator carrier, and broader operator-ideal commutator theory are classical and are correctly treated as prior art. Current searches did not locate the particular gauge Gamma_{p,q}(T)=inf ||A||_p||B||_q together with the rank-free comparison Gamma≈||T||_r for normal targets. The estimate is nevertheless a short quantitative amplification of the classical rank-one construction once the balanced normal split is observed, so originality is appropriately narrow. Anderson's 1986 sequel 'Commutators in ideals of trace class operators II' remains a residual attribution risk: open-access routes did not expose readable text, and authorized Oxford retrieval produced a six-page PDF resource with no extractable text, so the paper is not claimed to have been read.

scientific_value.summary: The theorem turns a classical existence boundary into a normed factorization statement with constants independent of rank and spectral spread, identifying S_r as the natural target scale. The tensor-transfer mechanism is reusable for normal targets, while the statement correctly avoids injective infinite-rank compacts and trace-zero phase claims.
